Vibration (speaker)

40 Hz
0.5 g
How vibration is modelledThe whole cartridge (hopper, plate, belts) is shaken rigidly and sinusoidally; in the cartridge's frame that is an oscillating extra gravity on every pill, so lift-off, bouncing and walking along the walls all come out of the normal contact physics. Strength is peak acceleration; above ~1 g pills briefly leave the surfaces each cycle. A 23 mm speaker at 40 Hz is far below its resonance and moves very little air — the real transmitted acceleration depends on how it is coupled to the frame, so measure it (phone accelerometer app on the cartridge) and set Strength to match.

Belt texture

Paint one tile of the belt surface. It repeats seamlessly around both belts and is part of the physics: ridges stand proud of the foam, grooves are cut into it, and their flanks push pills sideways / along. Arrow = direction of belt travel.

Geometry

Swap in your own parts. Mesh files: STL (binary or ASCII) or OBJ, in mm, exported in the assembly coordinates of the STEP so they land in place.
Cam file conventions2-D files (DXF / CSV): origin = cam shaft centre, units mm, +X points across the nip toward the other belt, +Y points up the incline toward the hopper; drawn as it sits at the start of a run. The belt wraps the cam taut, so only the outer (convex) envelope matters. The same profile drives both cams (cam B is the mirror image, as in the CAD). STL/OBJ cams are recognised either in assembly coordinates (sitting on cam A or B) or as a lone part with the shaft on its Z axis.

FoamFeed — what you are looking at

Your STEP assembly, simulated: pills dropped in the hopper funnel are pulled by the two counter-rotating foam belts into the 5 mm gap, where the two 2-lobe cams (tied together by the worm) squeeze the belts together twice per revolution so pills are gripped, metered and separated before they drop out of the bottom.

  • Foam: pick a material, then drag Hardness and Thickness while it runs. The curve shows the stress–strain law (elastic → plateau → densification) with the unloading branch dashed.
  • Plastic set: strains beyond the crush strain leave a permanent dent (part recovers with the recovery time, part never). It is stored on the belt material, so dents ride around the loop. Belts turn orange where they are worn; the map in the right panel shows it unrolled.
  • Pills: shape, size, density, bounciness and friction. Friction vs foam is multiplied by the foam grip factor and rises with squeeze.
  • Dispensing counts pills that leave through the bottom; "Doubles" are pills less than 80 ms behind another. Use Export dispense log for the timestamps.
  • Mouse: drag = orbit, right-drag or shift-drag = pan, wheel = zoom. Section cut slices the model to look inside.

Foam and friction values are engineering estimates, not measurements: calibrate hardness-to-modulus and the crush/recovery numbers with compression tests of your actual foam before trusting absolute numbers. Foam-on-foam contact (belts touching each other) is not modelled.
